state.track2_kraus_escalation: Kraus modular sieve escalation: p in [30001, 35000] and [35001, 40000] against newforms 72a1 and 144a1
state.track3_formal_proof: Ellenberg Q-curve modular descent for (4,4,p) over Z[i], Frey-Prym coverings, and Baker-Wustholz height bound B_0(p,q,r)

ellenberg_q_curve_descent.instructions: Does Ellenberg's Q-curve modular descent over Q(i) unconditionally eliminate primitive solutions to x^4 + y^4 = z^p for all sufficiently large prime exponents p?

criteria.true: Twists of Frey elliptic curves over Q(i) have trivial conductor outside {2} and their Galois representations cannot match any modular Hilbert/Bianchi form
criteria.false: Surviving non-trivial modular forms with rational coefficients remain over Q(i)

baker_wustholz_effective_closure.instructions: Does the explicit Baker-Wustholz theorem on linear forms in logarithms provide an effective, computable upper bound B_0 on the solutions of any fixed Beal signature (p, q, r) with 1/p + 1/q + 1/r < 1?

criteria.true: The logarithmic height h(P) is bounded effectively by a computable constant depending only on p, q, r, reducing the signature to finite search
criteria.false: Linear forms in logarithms cannot bound the heights of rational points on Darmon-Granville coverings

kraus_sieve_40k_scaling.instructions: What is the anticipated behavior of the Kraus sieve on p in [30001, 40000] against newforms 72a1 and 144a1?

criteria.100_percent: 100% elimination rate achieved with small multipliers k <= 50
criteria.partial_elimination: Elimination requires k > 100 for some primes
